etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English a(d)monisshen, perhaps from unnatested Old French *amonir + -ishen (modern English -ish), from Latin admoneō (“to remind, warn”), with regular shift of conjugation, itself from ad- + moneō (“to warn, advise”). Cognate with Italian ammonire and Portuguese amonir. Compare Middle English amonesten and French admonester.
senses: (transitive) To inform or notify of a fault; to rebuke in a serious tone; to tell off.
